text:
ana: Nightly profiler flagged steady KV cache growth on long-context workload (3h run). RSS +52% vs baseline. Heap sampling shows a huge count of small live allocations in the 128B-512B range. suspect fragmentation + reuse churn. link: https://oss.internal/kv/heap/1771239876

mike: Can you paste the hot alloc/caller stack and a short kv hist?

ana: (typo) here's the `kvstats --hist` snapshot from the run:
```
size_bin bytes  count
64        64     2,112
128       128    34,912
256       256    71,004
512       512    28,123
1024      1k     8,421
>1k      2048    1,102
```
Also attaching simplified backtrace summary: `alloc -> kv_slot_alloc -> kv_alloc_from_slab -> runtime_alloc` (most hot).

jin: Looks like our allocator is rounding small variable-sized KV entries into a narrow set of slot classes (256B/512B). For long-contexts we accumulate many half-used slots. Two levers: (1) adaptive grain sizes (split hot classes to include 192/320 sizes), or (2) background relinker/merge that rewrites live KV pages into denser slabs during idle.

sarah: FWIW I simulated the workload with a toy relinker and variable grain sizes. Results: adaptive grain + occasional relink cut resident by ~15% median, worst-case 22%. Cost: minor CPU for relink and small p50 token latency bump if relink runs inline.

mike: Any quick numbers on perf/regressions?

perf-bot: perf-nightly: longcontext-3h run
- memory: baseline 18.3GB -> candidate 15.6GB (-14.8%)
- p50 token latency: baseline 11.4ms -> candidate 11.7ms (+2.6%)
- p99 token latency: unchanged
(see: https://perf.internal/compare/1771239876)

sarah: Proposal:
- Introduce an "adaptive-grain" allocator flag behind runtime toggle. It creates mid-size bins for heavy small-object regimes and prefers compaction-friendly size families.
- Add a background relinker that: samples hot KV keys, copies them into dense pages, frees sparse pages. Run budgeted every 5m, 10ms budget per cycle.
- Add two metrics: `kv.fragmentation_ratio` (live_bytes / dense_bytes_est) and `kv.relink_ops`

jin: Implementation notes: allocator change should be lock-free on hot path (change only class selection math). Relinker can use existing GC worker threads; will do incremental copying to avoid latency cliffs.

ana: Questions: how to decide candidate keys for relink? I used access-frequency + age > 30m in sim. That avoided copying ephemeral keys.

jin: Yeah age+freq is fine. Start with: freq > 1000 tokens over 30m AND occupancy < 60% for page.

mike: Risk mitigation: feature gate, gradual canary on dedicated pool, observed metric dashboards and automatic rollback if p50/token > +10% or fragmentation_ratio increases.

devops-bot: scheduled canary: redwood-dedicated-3 at 2024-10-11T03:00:00Z (flag adaptive-grain=true, relinker=budgeted)

perf-bot: quick canary run (10m sample): mem -9%, p50 +0.3% -> within safe window

ana: Action items:
- jin: open PR for allocator class selection math + tests (owner: jin)
- ana: push long-context sim harness and baseline artifacts to the perf dashboard (owner: ana)
- sarah: propose dashboard panels and alert thresholds for fragmentation_ratio and relink_ops (owner: sarah)
- mike: coordinate canary and rollback runbooks (owner: mike)

jin: I'll start the PR today, will include microbench and stress harness.

ana: I'll add regression scenario that simulates long conversations and attach memory traces.

mike: Sounds good. Please tag me on PRs. Let's keep the default off until canary proves stable. :thumbsup:

sarah: Thanks all — if no objections I'll create the RFC doc this afternoon with the sim graphs and a rough timeline.

ana: no objections from me, thanks.

mike: ack
